newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER WELCOMES DALGLISH WITH CUP WINNER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER WELCOMES DALGLISH WITH CUP WINNER.

text.p: England striker Alan Shearer welcomed new manager Kenny Dalglish to Newcastle United with the winning goal in their F.A.Cup third-round replay against Charlton on Wednesday.
Shearer scored in the 10th minute of extra time as his premier league team beat their first division rivals from south London 2-1.
Dalglish, who was appointed on Tuesday following Kevin Keegan's resignation as manager last week, went out on to the pitch to be welcomed by the crowd before the game.
The former Liverpool and Blackburn manager was at St James' Park essentially as a spectator, leaving caretaker managers Terry McDermott and Arthur Cox to take charge of the team for the Cup replay.
Midfielder Lee Clark thrust Newcastle ahead after 33 minutes but Charlton hit back when midfielder Mark Robson scored direct from a free kick in the 55th minute.
However, England captain Shearer's extra-time winner, also direct from a free kick, sent Newcastle into a fourth-round home tie against Nottingham Forest.
A high-quality goal from Dutch international Dennis Bergkamp set Arsenal on their way to a 2-0 victory in a third round replay at Sunderland.
Bergkamp, sent off when the London club were beaten 1-0 in Saturday's premier league clash at Sunderland, fired Arsenal ahead in the first minute of the second half.
The Dutchman cut out an attempted clearance, adroitly eluded a challenge and scored with a beautifully-weighted rising shot into the far corner of the net.
Arsenal sealed victory after 65 minutes when a cross from the right by Paul Merson was headed home by diving midfielder Stephen Hughes for his first senior goal for the club.
The Londoners now face the winners of a third round replay between Leeds and Crystal Palace.
Premier league Leicester accounted for first division Southend 2-0 in a third round home tie.
Ian Marshall created the first goal for striker Steve Claridge after 40 minutes and scored the second himself three minutes after halftime.
Second division Stockport, already in the League Cup quarter-finals, went through to the fourth round by ousting Stoke 2-0 away thanks to goals from Keiron Durkan and Alun Armstrong.
